BACKPORT: FROMGIT: arm64: dts: rockchip: Add 32k clk on rk3399-gru This adds the 32k clock to the RK3399 Gru board file, which is provided by a Silego oscillator on Gru boards. Even though it's not directly used, muxes will end up traversing the entire clk tree on calls to determine_rate if it doesn't exist. This is because the 32k clk is listed as a possible parent on some clks. Since the clk doesn't know about the 32k clk (it was never registered), it triggers a global search for it. This can happen about 40 times per second, which isn't great for power. Signed-off-by: Derek Basehore <dbasehore@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> [moved clock position and adapted commit message a bit] Signed-off-by: Heiko Stuebner <heiko@sntech.de> (cherry picked from commit 17222eb932ad2ec67e583179f507982460d81bde https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/mmind/linux-rockchip.git/ for-next) Conflicts: [Context delta] arch/arm64/boot/dts/rockchip/rk3399-gru.dtsi BUG=b:120160928 TEST=boot kevin Change-Id: Id52c4bf5ef569e2158b7c7b2ddc07d6018ec7f92 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1354522 Commit-Ready: Derek Basehore <dbasehore@chromium.org> Tested-by: Derek Basehore <dbasehore@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: cros_ec: handle MKBP more events flag CL:1341159 adds a "more events" flag to allow the EC to notify us that there are more MKBP events waiting to be served. This CL extends the cros_ec bottom-half IRQ handler to listen to that flag in order to try and serve all known events before returning to the kernel with IRQ_HANDLED. This serves an optimization purpose as it minimizes the round-trip back and forth from the interrupt handler, and it also improves the quality of sensor timestamping, as it avoids a mismatch of event times between EC and AP that can confuse the median filter we use in the sensor ring. As described in the EC CL, this change is forward and backward compatible. BUG=b:119570064, b:112102925 TEST=on nocturne, enable sensors and use hardware buttons and observe the kernel receive MKBP events with the flag enabled Change-Id: I1a924bfe0255367329f7a07d4e2b62af2709efa1 Signed-off-by: Enrico Granata <egranata@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1340983 Commit-Ready: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org> Tested-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org>
